newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude and products to test resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude and products to test resistance.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Short-covering ahead of the weekend and against expiring July options could lead the market up to as high as $19.50 temporarily.
* Some tests of resistance may be seen on crude and products contracts, but selling into the rallies could limit any upside.
NYMEX crude and products futures are seen holding steady on Friday, but though some tests of resistance may be seen, selling into the rallies could limit any upside, analysts say.
However, brokers said short-covering ahead of the weekend and against expiring July options could lead the market up to as high as or even provide a break of $19.50 temporarily.

"WTI (NYMEX crude) will be looking to test resistance at $19 and $19.20 a break of which could take us above $20 and may even test the 40-day moving average line at $20.30," Darren Gurner at Sucden said,
However, he warned that failure to break above resistance could push the market back down to $18.41 support.

Charles Gray at Prudential Bache said that stochastics on the NYMEX chart for all the contracts have crossed over, flagging a buy signal. "The overall feeling of a loss of momentum to the downside is also giving some support to the current levels," he said.

Victor Yu at Refco in New York saw the $19.50 a barrel level, that the options expiry offers, as "more realistic" for the market at this time of year and if achieved he expected that products would be pulled higher too.
"If WTI can continue to build on it's recent stability for more than a day or so there is a chance of a move up that could also take gasoline back to 60 cents," Yu said.
"Gasoline has shrugged off the bearish API/DOE stats and we may now see a test of it's underlying strength," he added, pointing to 58.70 cents as the first point of solid resistance.

Gurner said heating oil remains in consolidation mode but saw the possibility of the market bouncing up to test resistance at $52.50 and the 40 day moving average at 54.67 cents a gallon on the July contract.
